notes: PMOS: the NHS about-metformin text retrieved says the NHS now uses polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) in place of PCOS (polycystic ovary syndrome). Final text names both so readers recognise either; this differs from the site entry in content/medications.json (which says polycystic ovary syndrome, off label) and from the first-pass wording only in adding the older name. Reviewer should decide whether the site-wide term should change. Breastfeeding: NHS says it can be taken if the baby is healthy; a PMC review of manufacturer labels says labels advise against; both are described, neither instructs. Kidney sentence: reworded to 'the doctor checks kidney function regularly' (leaflets); the 'before starting' claim was only in a trial protocol and was cut. Gestational diabetes sentence is no longer treated as textbook; NHS trust pages (Guy's and St Thomas') support it. Dorset hospital leaflet attribution removed; the alone-or-with-insulin claim removed. Search summaries blend pages, so URLs for some NHS claims are the main metformin page or the nearest NHS metformin page (the side effects subpage was not returned by search); the leaflet URL for the contrast-dye sentence (emc pil.13161) is the best match but the summary did not name the exact leaflet. 'The NHS asks people who drink heavily to tell the doctor' rests on the who-can-and-cannot summary. Existing site entry also says dose/eGFR/HbA1c numbers that were not rechecked here (outside this article). Eight searches used.
